transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, doctor. I'm here because I have an intense, overwhelming fear of elevators and enclosed spaces that is making it very difficult to go about my daily life. It has gotten to the point where it is severely restricting my routine, and I really need help managing it.
When you are in these enclosed spaces, are you primarily afraid of the space itself, or are you concerned that you might have a panic attack and be unable to escape or get help?

I'm not entirely sure about the exact distinction, to be honest. It feels like a mix of both because the tight space itself terrifies me, but I also dread the feeling of being trapped and panicking with no way out.
Do you find that you experience this same level of intense worry about many different areas of your life—such as your health, work, or finances—even when you are not in an enclosed space?

No, I don't experience that kind of intense worry about other parts of my life like my health, work, or finances. My extreme fear is really just focused on enclosed spaces. Aside from that, I generally feel fine.

latest_inference.note: The patient explicitly denied experiencing the pervasive, excessive worry about multiple life domains (health, work, finances) that is characteristic of Generalized Anxiety Disorder. Given that their anxiety is specifically and exclusively focused on enclosed spaces (elevators), Specific Phobia is now the most appropriate candidate.
